plainTranslation:
Support in this connection grows when you actually let each other in.

There's a natural sense of goodwill here. This person wants good things for you, and you probably want the same for them. But the closeness doesn't happen automatically. It builds little by little, every time you share something real and find that it's met with care instead of judgment.

What makes this connection special isn't some huge emotional breakthrough. It's the small stuff. Feeling listened to. Feeling remembered. Knowing someone notices when you're having a hard time. Realizing you don't have to handle everything on your own.

Because the support is gentle rather than overwhelming, it's easy to miss. You might assume they know what's going on without ever saying it. You might keep things to yourself until you're already struggling, then wonder why the connection doesn't feel as supportive as it could.

The more you let this person be part of your emotional world, the stronger the bond becomes. The more honest you are about what's going on, the more room there is for real support. What starts as simple kindness can grow into something deeply comforting and reliable over time.
